units.translation: who will not allow the tongue to nourish evils.
pouring vinegar and oil into the same vessel,

[The verse quoted by Plutarch in the Lives of Alcibiades c. 4, Pelopidas c. 29 and Moralia p. 762f, ἔπτηξ' ἀλέκτωρ δοῦλον ὡς κλίνας πτερόν [the rooster cowered, lowering its wing like a slave], Hermann plausibly attributes to Aeschylus in his note on the Fragments p. 410.]
boast confidently, like a rooster near his hens.
the rooster cowered, lowering its wing like a slave,
there was no remedy, neither edible, nor ointment, nor trustworthy.
Hesychius ἀλαιός· ὁ παλαιός, ἄφρων [alaios: the old, foolish]. Aeschylus (fr. 409). But rather ἀλεός [aleos]: see Herodian on anomalous words p. 4, 19. schol. Arist. Lys. 988. Etym. M. p. 59, 45.
